nodes.summary: Numba kernel implementing the EMA alert-and-carry entry logic: an alert bar straddling the EMA arms an entry at its high/low, carried across bars within the same day until triggered or invalidated.

nodes.name: EMASignals
nodes.summary: Dataclass container for generated EMA signals: entry mask, direction, entry/stop prices, and the alert bar index series.

nodes.name: generate_signals_for_frame
nodes.summary: Top-level EMA signal generator for one OHLC frame: computes the EMA, runs the alert-carry kernel for the requested direction, and optionally suppresses entries during detected range shifts.

nodes.name: _detect_range_shift
nodes.summary: Detects rolling-range breakout shifts (new highs above prior range high or lows below prior range low) used to gate EMA entries.

nodes.name: exits.py
nodes.summary: ORB trade exit engine: a large Numba simulation loop walks each entry forward applying stop/target, time stop, failed-breakout, volatility-trail, and opposite-break exits, wrapped by a pandas-facing apply_exits API that builds the trades DataFrame.
nodes.languageNotes: simulate_trades takes 22 flat scalar/array params because Numba nopython mode cannot accept dicts — apply_exits unpacks the config dict into them.

nodes.name: simulate_trades
nodes.summary: Numba-compiled per-trade simulation: from each entry bar, walks forward applying stop-loss, profit target, max-hold, time-stop, failed-breakout, volatility-trail, and opposite-OR-break exits with slippage, returning exit bar/price/reason arrays.

nodes.name: apply_exits
nodes.summary: Pandas-facing wrapper that unpacks the ORB config dict, computes ATR and time-cutoff masks, flattens long/short entry coordinates, runs simulate_trades, and assembles the resulting trades DataFrame with mapped exit reasons.

nodes.name: regime_filter.py
nodes.summary: Market regime classification and gating for ORB trades: labels each (date, symbol) as trend/chop/high-vol/low-vol/wide-OR/narrow-OR from daily ATR, chop crossings, and OR width, then filters trades and reports per-regime expectancy.
nodes.languageNotes: Regime labels are shifted by one day before gating to avoid lookahead — only the prior day's regime is tradeable.

nodes.name: chop_cross_count
nodes.summary: Numba kernel counting how many times intraday close crosses the day's midpoint per symbol per day, used as the chop-regime indicator.

nodes.name: classify_regimes
nodes.summary: Builds the full regime dictionary: aggregates intraday bars to daily OHLC, computes daily ATR percentile bands, chop cross counts, trend range percentage, and OR-width multiples, then assigns shifted regime labels per (date, symbol).

nodes.name: get_primary_regime
nodes.summary: Looks up the primary (first-listed) regime label for a given date and symbol from the regime dictionary.

nodes.name: apply_regime_gate
nodes.summary: Filters a trades DataFrame by regime: drops trades whose entry-day regime appears in skip_regimes or is absent from require_regimes.

nodes.name: compute_regime_expectancy
nodes.summary: Computes mean PnL (expectancy) of trades grouped by their primary regime label, returning a regime-to-expectancy mapping for diagnostics.

nodes.name: research.py
nodes.summary: Declares ORB_RESEARCH_SPEC, the FamilyResearchSpec for the ORB family: an LLM-facing config schema text listing all supported keys and defaults, research questions, config rules, allowed key set, and concept-regex mappings for hypothesis-config alignment scoring.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure module-level declaration — the schema text is f-string-built from canonical_regimes() and supported_config_keys() so the prompt can never drift from the runtime-validated key list.

nodes.name: schema.py
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for ORB configuration vocabulary: canonical regime names with alias normalization, the supported config-key whitelist, and validators that reject unsupported keys and normalize regime lists.

nodes.name: normalize_regime_name
nodes.summary: Maps a regime name through the alias table to its canonical form, raising ValueError for unknown names.

nodes.name: normalize_config_changes
nodes.summary: Validates that proposed config_changes only contain supported keys and normalizes skip_regimes/require_regimes lists to canonical regime names, raising ValueError on unsupported keys.

nodes.name: validate_runtime_config
nodes.summary: Validates a full runtime ORB config in place: rejects unsupported keys and canonicalizes regime list values before the backtest runs.

nodes.name: signals.py
nodes.summary: ORB entry-signal engine: computes per-day opening ranges, median OR width, relative-volume gates, and trend/volume/wide-OR/follow-through filters, producing long/short breakout entries with stop and target prices in the ORBSignals container.
nodes.languageNotes: Thin private wrappers (_day_ids, _bar_of_day, _first_signal_per_day) bridge pandas indexes into the shared Numba kernels from numba_kernels.py.

nodes.name: ORBSignals
nodes.summary: Dataclass container for generated ORB signals: long/short entry masks, stop/target prices, opening-range high/low/width frames, and the relative-volume series.

nodes.name: compute_opening_range
nodes.summary: Computes each trading day's opening-range high, low, and width from the first N minutes of bars and broadcasts them across all bars of the day.

nodes.name: compute_median_or_width
nodes.summary: Computes the trailing-lookback median opening-range width per symbol, used as the baseline for wide/narrow OR filters.

nodes.name: compute_rvol_gate
nodes.summary: Computes a relative-volume gate: today's opening-window volume versus a trailing mean/median baseline, returning a boolean mask requiring rvol above the threshold with sufficient history.

nodes.name: generate_orb_signals
nodes.summary: Top-level ORB signal generator: reads ~20 config keys, computes opening ranges and filters (volume, trend EMA, wide-OR, follow-through, rvol gate), detects breakout entries above/below the OR, caps one entry per day, and returns an ORBSignals bundle with stop/target prices.

nodes.name: migrate_experiment_dirs.py
nodes.summary: One-shot migration script that renames per-round experiment directories to the research_round_id naming scheme by loading the thesis/job/round mapping from backtest-run SQLite databases, detecting collisions, planning and executing renames with marker files, and rewriting stored paths in the databases.

nodes.name: ExplicitDbMissingError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when an explicitly specified backtest-run database path does not exist on disk.

nodes.name: _discover_db_paths
nodes.summary: Resolves backtest-run database paths from explicit CLI arguments (raising ExplicitDbMissingError on missing files) or by recursive glob discovery under the runtime root, deduplicating results.

nodes.name: _load_mapping
nodes.summary: Queries each SQLite database's backtest_runs table for (thesis_id, job, research_round_number) keys mapped to research_round_id values, skipping malformed rows with warnings.

nodes.name: _detect_collisions
nodes.summary: Finds mapping keys that resolve to more than one research_round_id, returning the ambiguous entries so the migration can abort instead of renaming inconsistently.

nodes.name: _iter_experiment_subdirs
nodes.summary: Walks runtime/jobs/job-N/research/round-M/experiments directories using regex-matched dir names and yields each experiment subdirectory with its job and round numbers.

nodes.name: _build_lookups
nodes.summary: Builds forward (key to round id) and reverse (round id to key) lookup dicts from the mapping, raising ValueError if a round id maps back to multiple keys.

nodes.name: _plan_renames
nodes.summary: Compares each on-disk experiment subdirectory name against the lookup tables and produces the list of planned renames (forward or reverse mode) plus directories with no known mapping.

nodes.name: _execute_renames
nodes.summary: Performs the planned directory renames, refusing to overwrite existing targets, removing stale marker files, and touching a migration marker in each renamed directory for idempotency.

nodes.name: _rewrite_db_paths
nodes.summary: Updates stored artifact path columns in each SQLite database to reflect the executed directory renames, committing per database and counting rewritten rows.

nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses arguments (root, explicit DBs, dry-run, reverse), discovers databases, loads the mapping, aborts on collisions, plans renames, then executes renames and rewrites DB paths unless in dry-run mode.

nodes.name: resolve_chunk_path

nodes.name: main

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Re-anchor on the README's loop narrative: each iteration plans the next thesis from prior results, has the conductor agent research a structured thesis, compiles missing strategy primitives, backtests the config, and feeds findings into the next round. The five-plane architecture (entry, orchestration, agent, compiler, backtest) plus trace and persistence is the map the rest of this tour follows.

tour.title: Controller State Machine
tour.description: autoresearch_controller.py is the single long-lived process: a per-family state machine that decides, each tick, whether to plan, research, compile, backtest, or halt. autoresearch_orchestration.py holds the state-transition helpers it leans on — resume logic, baseline rerun, and next-action selection — so the controller file stays a readable loop rather than a tangle of branches. BFS confirms everything else in the repo hangs off this node (14 direct imports).

tour.title: Shared Foundations and State
tour.description: Before following the loop, recall where state lives: autoresearch_state.py reads/writes the per-job state file (the controller's source of truth between ticks), backtest_run_db.py is the SQLite record of every backtest run keyed by research_round_id, and persistence_utils.py (fan-in 19) is the shared atomic-write layer beneath both. autoresearch_logging.py (fan-in 32) and autoresearch_constants.py (fan-in 16) are the two most-depended-on files in the repo — every plane logs and names things through them.

tour.title: Planning: Choosing the Next Thesis
tour.description: Step one of the loop. autoresearch_planning.py generates thesis candidates from prior experiment results and decides what to attempt next; thesis_validator.py enforces the hard gates a thesis must pass (structured config changes, expected effects, disqualifiers) before it is allowed into a research round. Remember the recent invariant: thesis IDs are assigned from research attempts and attempt history is canonicalized here.

tour.title: Research Rounds and the Conductor
tour.description: autoresearch_research.py runs a per-thesis research round on behalf of the controller, delegating to research_conductor.py — the agent that actually drives sub-agent calls (web, code, data) and assembles the structured thesis payload. research_types.py defines the Pydantic shapes that flow between them; normalization must happen at every model_validate call site (rule B), which is why these types are centralized.

tour.title: Sub-Agents, MCP Tools, and Memory
tour.description: The conductor's workforce: research_subagents.py defines the individual agents, research_tools_mcp.py exposes the MCP tool surface they call (all args Pydantic-validated as of PR #63), and research_memory.py is the MemPalace bridge that carries findings across sessions so each round starts informed rather than cold.

tour.title: Agent Plane Infrastructure
tour.description: Beneath the research layer sits the generic agent machinery: agent_orchestrator.py is the public API (diagnostics, web research, thesis), agent_runners.py implements the runners, agent_openai_calls.py wraps the OpenAI API with retry and token tracking, and agent_infra.py (fan-in 8) holds the shared clients. Every LLM call in the system funnels through this stack, which is what makes the token audit in Step 12 possible.

tour.title: Compiler Plane
tour.description: When a validated thesis references strategy primitives that don't exist yet, compiler_pipeline.py orchestrates the build: compiler_builder.py has builder agents generate the missing code, compiler_operationalize.py wires the compiled strategy into runnable form, and compiler_thesis_io.py handles thesis read/write at the boundary. This is the bridge between 'agent proposed it' and 'backtest can run it'.

tour.title: Strategy Families
tour.description: strategies/base.py provides the @register decorator and the STRATEGIES dict — the one home for family registration (fan-in 12). strategy_family.py is the controller-facing abstraction over a family, and the ema/ and orb/ packages are the two concrete registrants, each bundling its own config validation, research prompt, and exits. Adding a family means copying strategies/_demo, not touching the controller.
tour.languageLesson: The registry pattern via decorator (@register populating a module-level STRATEGIES dict at import time) means strategies/__init__.py must import each family package for registration to fire — a silent failure mode if a new family forgets the import.

tour.title: Backtest Engine and Evaluation
tour.description: The compiled config runs here: backtest/runner.py executes the backtest over data loaded via backtest/data_universe.py under backtest/runtime_config.py. autoresearch_experiment.py logs the run and evaluates metrics through eval_metrics.py (fan-in 6), producing the verdict that planning consumes next iteration — closing the loop you started at Step 4.

tour.title: Trace and Self-Improvement
tour.description: trace_sdk.py (fan-in 22, second only to logging) defines the trace event schema and writer that every plane emits into; the trace_adapters package (halo, recursive_improve, reflexio) transforms raw traces per improvement framework — the graph's tightest cluster (13 internal edges), so read them together. agent_token_usage.py turns each LLM call into a trace event, and improvement_reflexion.py consumes traces to feed reflections back into future rounds. Remember rule H/instrumentation discipline: all of this is fail-open and never blocks the business loop.

tour.title: Configuration Surface
tour.description: configs/ema_base.yaml and configs/orb_base.yaml are the baseline strategy configs that theses mutate — a thesis is literally a structured diff against these. .env.example documents the required environment (data root, VPS SSH target, Discord webhooks), and pyproject.toml pins the toolchain. Tunables live here, not hardcoded, per the config-smell rule.
tour.languageLesson: Env-var tunables are read through lazy accessor functions rather than module-level constants, so pytest monkeypatch.setenv works regardless of import order.

tour.title: Deploy, CLI, and CI
tour.description: The operational shell around the loop: vps_runner.py deploys a git ref to the VPS and launches the controller remotely; autoresearch_cli.py is the SQLite-backed experiment-tracking CLI (init/log/status) over the same run DB from Step 3; scripts/token_audit.py slices the token-usage traces by model, agent, or job after a run. The CI workflow is the canonical test gate — the full suite runs in GitHub Actions, not locally.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions: the CI workflow is watched via 'gh run watch --exit-status' as the project's required verification step before any change is considered done.
